title: 09. Deep Learning: RNN Fundamentals
summary: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) process sequential data by maintaining hidden state across time steps. Unlike feedforward networks, RNNs have loops that allow information to persist.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
**Status:** ✅ COMPLETE  
**Last Updated:** December 6, 2025

**Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)** process sequential data by maintaining hidden state across time steps. Unlike feedforward networks, RNNs have loops that allow information to persist.

### What You'll Learn:
- Sequential data and temporal dependencies
- RNN architecture and equations
- Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)
- Vanishing/exploding gradient problem
- PyTorch RNN implementation

sections.title: 1. Why RNNs?
sections.body:
### Sequential Data Everywhere:

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import numpy as np

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("SEQUENTIAL DATA AND RNNS")
print("="*70)

print("""
Sequential Data Examples:
   📝 Text: "The cat sat on the ___"
   📈 Time Series: Stock prices, weather, sensor data
   🎵 Audio: Speech recognition, music generation
   🎬 Video: Frame sequences
   💬 Conversations: Chatbots, dialogue systems

Key Challenge: Order matters!
   • "Dog bites man" ≠ "Man bites dog"
   • Context from previous words/timesteps is crucial
   • Variable-length sequences

Why Not CNNs?
   ❌ Fixed receptive field
   ❌ No memory of distant past
   ❌ Position-dependent (not sequence-aware)

Why Not Feedforward Networks?
   ❌ Fixed input size
   ❌ No parameter sharing across time
   ❌ Millions of parameters for long sequences

RNN Solution:
   ✅ Variable-length sequences
   ✅ Parameter sharing across time
   ✅ Memory through hidden state
   ✅ Process one element at a time
""")

print("="*70)
```

sections.title: 2. RNN Architecture
sections.body:
### The Core Mechanism:

```python
print("\n" + "="*70)
print("RNN ARCHITECTURE")
print("="*70)

print("""
RNN Unfolded Through Time:

        h₀      h₁      h₂      h₃
        ↓       ↓       ↓       ↓
   ┌────┴───┬───┴───┬───┴───┬───┴───┐
   │  RNN   │  RNN  │  RNN  │  RNN  │
   └────┬───┴───┬───┴───┬───┴───┬───┘
        ↑       ↑       ↑       ↑
        x₀      x₁      x₂      x₃

At each timestep t:
   h_t = tanh(W_hh · h_{t-1} + W_xh · x_t + b_h)
   y_t = W_hy · h_t + b_y

Components:
   • x_t: Input at time t
   • h_t: Hidden state at time t (memory!)
   • y_t: Output at time t
   • W_hh: Hidden-to-hidden weights
   • W_xh: Input-to-hidden weights
   • W_hy: Hidden-to-output weights

Key Insight: Same weights W used at every timestep!
   → Parameter sharing across time
   → Can handle any sequence length

Hidden State h_t:
   • Summarizes all previous inputs
   • "Memory" of the sequence
   • Passed to next timestep
   • Enables long-range dependencies
""")

# Vanilla RNN implementation
class VanillaRNN(nn.Module):
    """Simple RNN from scratch."""
    
    def __init__(self, input_size, hidden_size, output_size):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        
        # Weights
        self.W_xh = nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size)
        self.W_hh = nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size)
        self.W_hy = nn.Linear(hidden_size, output_size)
        
        self.tanh = nn.Tanh()
    
    def forward(self, x, h_prev=None):
        """
        Args:
            x: (batch, seq_len, input_size)
            h_prev: (batch, hidden_size) or None
        
        Returns:
            outputs: (batch, seq_len, output_size)
            h_t: (batch, hidden_size)
        """
        batch_size, seq_len, _ = x.size()
        
        # Initialize hidden state
        if h_prev is None:
            h_t = torch.zeros(batch_size, self.hidden_size)
        else:
            h_t = h_prev
        
        outputs = []
        
        # Process sequence
        for t in range(seq_len):
            x_t = x[:, t, :]  # Input at time t
            
            # RNN update
            h_t = self.tanh(self.W_xh(x_t) + self.W_hh(h_t))
            
            # Output
            y_t = self.W_hy(h_t)
            outputs.append(y_t)
        
        # Stack outputs
        outputs = torch.stack(outputs, dim=1)  # (batch, seq_len, output)
        
        return outputs, h_t

# Test
print("\n💻 Testing Vanilla RNN:")
rnn = VanillaRNN(input_size=10, hidden_size=20, output_size=5)
x = torch.randn(8, 15, 10)  # Batch=8, SeqLen=15, Features=10

outputs, final_hidden = rnn(x)
print(f"Input: {x.shape}")
print(f"Outputs: {outputs.shape}")
print(f"Final hidden: {final_hidden.shape}")

print("="*70)
```

diagrams.title: RNNs and the LSTM memory cell
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  x1["x1"] --> h1["hidden state h1"]
  h1 --> h2["h2"]
  x2["x2"] --> h2
  h2 --> h3["h3"]
  x3["x3"] --> h3
  h3 --> y["output"]
  lstm["LSTM gates — forget, input, output — decide what the cell state keeps"] -.-> h2
diagrams.explain: An RNN reads a sequence one step at a time, carrying a hidden state forward, but plain RNNs forget long-range information because gradients vanish over many steps. LSTMs and GRUs add gates that learn what to keep and what to forget. Transformers have largely replaced them by attending to all positions at once.

sections.title: 3. Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)
sections.body:
### Training RNNs:

```python
print("BACKPROPAGATION THROUGH TIME")
```

Challenge: How to compute gradients through sequence?

BPTT: Unroll RNN through time, then backprop!

**Forward Pass:**
```python
t=0: h₀ = tanh(W_hh·h_{-1} + W_xh·x₀)
t=1: h₁ = tanh(W_hh·h₀ + W_xh·x₁)
t=2: h₂ = tanh(W_hh·h₁ + W_xh·x₂)
```
...
```python
t=T: h_T = tanh(W_hh·h_{T-1} + W_xh·x_T)
```

**Backward Pass (chain rule):**
∂L/∂W_hh = Σ_t ∂L_t/∂W_hh

But each ∂L_t/∂W_hh depends on all previous timesteps!

∂h_t/∂h_{t-1} = W_hh · diag(1 - h_t²)  [tanh derivative]

∂L/∂h₀ = ∂L/∂h_T · ∂h_T/∂h_{T-1} · ... · ∂h₁/∂h₀

Problem: Long chains of multiplications!
- If |∂h_t/∂h_{t-1}| < 1 → Vanishing gradients
- If |∂h_t/∂h_{t-1}| > 1 → Exploding gradients

**Gradient after T steps:**
∂L/∂h₀ ∝ (W_hh)^T

If largest eigenvalue λ:
- λ < 1: Gradient → 0 (vanishing)
- λ > 1: Gradient → ∞ (exploding)

Typical: λ(W_hh) ~ 1.0 → But tanh squashes → Vanishing!

```python
# Demonstrate gradient flow
def analyze_gradient_flow(seq_length=50):
    """Show vanishing gradient problem."""
    
    # Simulate gradient backprop
    W = 0.9  # Weight < 1
    gradient = 1.0
    gradients = [gradient]
    
    for t in range(seq_length):
        gradient = gradient * W
        gradients.append(gradient)
    
    print(f"\n📉 Gradient Flow (W={W}):")
    print(f"   t=0:  gradient = {gradients[0]:.6f}")
    print(f"   t=10: gradient = {gradients[10]:.6f}")
    print(f"   t=25: gradient = {gradients[25]:.6f}")
    print(f"   t=50: gradient = {gradients[50]:.6f}")
    print(f"   → Vanished to {gradients[50]:.2e}! ❌")

analyze_gradient_flow()
```

**Consequences:**
- Can't learn long-term dependencies
- Only recent timesteps influence learning
- "Memory" limited to ~10 timesteps

**Solutions (next topics):**
1. LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory)
2. GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit)
3. Gradient clipping
4. Better initialization
5. Skip connections

sections.title: 4. PyTorch RNN Implementation
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- import torch import torch.nn as nn
- Input: (batch, seq_len, input_size)
- X: (batch, seq_len) - token indices
- Embed: (batch, seq_len, embed_dim)
- RNN: (batch, seq_len, hidden_dim)
- Use last hidden state for classification
- Decode (using encoder's final state)

**Defines:** `RNNClassifier`, `Seq2SeqRNN`

### Using Built-in RNNs:

```python
print("\n" + "="*70)
print("PYTORCH RNN LAYERS")
print("="*70)

pytorch_rnn = """
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# ============================================================
# BASIC RNN LAYER
# ============================================================

rnn = nn.RNN(
    input_size=10,      # Input feature dimension
    hidden_size=20,     # Hidden state dimension
    num_layers=2,       # Stack multiple RNN layers
    nonlinearity='tanh', # or 'relu'
    batch_first=True,   # Input shape: (batch, seq, features)
    dropout=0.5,        # Dropout between layers
    bidirectional=False # One direction
)

# Input: (batch, seq_len, input_size)
x = torch.randn(8, 15, 10)

# Forward pass
output, h_n = rnn(x)

print(f"Input: {x.shape}")           # (8, 15, 10)
print(f"Output: {output.shape}")     # (8, 15, 20) - hidden at each timestep
print(f"Final hidden: {h_n.shape}")  # (2, 8, 20) - 2 layers

# ============================================================
# COMPLETE RNN MODEL FOR SEQUENCE CLASSIFICATION
# ============================================================

class RNNClassifier(nn.Module):
    \"\"\"RNN for sequence classification.\"\"\"
    
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim, hidden_dim, num_classes):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Embedding layer
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        
        # RNN layer
        self.rnn = nn.RNN(
            embed_dim, 
            hidden_dim,
            num_layers=2,
            batch_first=True,
            dropout=0.5
        )
        
        # Classification head
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # x: (batch, seq_len) - token indices
        
        # Embed: (batch, seq_len, embed_dim)
        x = self.embedding(x)
        
        # RNN: (batch, seq_len, hidden_dim)
        output, h_n = self.rnn(x)
        
        # Use last hidden state for classification
        last_hidden = h_n[-1]  # Take top layer
        
        # Classify: (batch, num_classes)
        logits = self.fc(last_hidden)
        
        return logits

# Usage
model = RNNClassifier(vocab_size=5000, embed_dim=128, 
                     hidden_dim=256, num_classes=2)

# Example: Sentiment classification
sequences = torch.randint(0, 5000, (32, 50))  # 32 sentences, 50 tokens
predictions = model(sequences)

print(f"\\nSequences: {sequences.shape}")
print(f"Predictions: {predictions.shape}")  # (32, 2) - binary sentiment

# ============================================================
# RNN FOR SEQUENCE-TO-SEQUENCE
# ============================================================

class Seq2SeqRNN(nn.Module):
    \"\"\"RNN for sequence-to-sequence (e.g., machine translation).\"\"\"
    
    def __init__(self, input_vocab, output_vocab, embed_dim, hidden_dim):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Encoder
        self.encoder_embed = nn.Embedding(input_vocab, embed_dim)
        self.encoder_rnn = nn.RNN(embed_dim, hidden_dim, batch_first=True)
        
        # Decoder
        self.decoder_embed = nn.Embedding(output_vocab, embed_dim)
        self.decoder_rnn = nn.RNN(embed_dim, hidden_dim, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_vocab)
    
    def forward(self, src, tgt):
        # Encode
        src_embed = self.encoder_embed(src)
        _, encoder_hidden = self.encoder_rnn(src_embed)
        
        # Decode (using encoder's final state)
        tgt_embed = self.decoder_embed(tgt)
        decoder_output, _ = self.decoder_rnn(tgt_embed, encoder_hidden)
        
        # Project to vocabulary
        output = self.fc(decoder_output)
        
        return output

# Usage
seq2seq = Seq2SeqRNN(input_vocab=5000, output_vocab=5000,
                     embed_dim=128, hidden_dim=256)

src = torch.randint(0, 5000, (32, 20))  # Source sequences
tgt = torch.randint(0, 5000, (32, 25))  # Target sequences
output = seq2seq(src, tgt)

print(f"\\nSource: {src.shape}")
print(f"Target: {tgt.shape}")
print(f"Output: {output.shape}")  # (32, 25, 5000) - vocab logits
"""

print(pytorch_rnn)
print("="*70)
```

sections.title: 5. RNN Applications
sections.body:
### What RNNs Excel At:

```python
print("RNN APPLICATIONS")
```

**1. SEQUENCE CLASSIFICATION**
═══════════════════════════════════════
Input: Variable-length sequence
Output: Single label

**Examples:**
- Sentiment analysis: "Great movie!" → Positive
- Spam detection: Email text → Spam/Not spam
- Intent classification: "Book a flight" → Intent

**Architecture:**
Sequence → RNN → Last hidden → Dense → Label

**2. SEQUENCE LABELING**
═══════════════════════════════════════
Input: Sequence
Output: Label for each element

**Examples:**
- Part-of-speech tagging: "The/DET cat/NOUN sat/VERB"
- Named entity recognition: "John/PERSON lives in NYC/LOCATION"
- Video frame labeling

**Architecture:**
Sequence → RNN → Output at each step → Labels

**3. SEQUENCE GENERATION**
═══════════════════════════════════════
Input: Context
Output: Generated sequence

**Examples:**
- Text generation: "Once upon a time..." → story
- Music generation
- Handwriting synthesis

**Architecture:**
Start token → RNN → Sample → Feed back → Repeat

**4. SEQUENCE-TO-SEQUENCE**
═══════════════════════════════════════
Input: Source sequence
Output: Target sequence (different length!)

**Examples:**
- Machine translation: "Hello" → "Hola"
- Summarization: Long text → Short summary
- Speech recognition: Audio → Text

**Architecture:**
Source → Encoder RNN → Context → Decoder RNN → Target

**5. TIME SERIES FORECASTING**
═══════════════════════════════════════
Input: Historical data
Output: Future predictions

**Examples:**
- Stock price prediction
- Weather forecasting
- Energy demand prediction

**Architecture:**
History → RNN → Next values

```python
# Simple text generation example
class CharRNN(nn.Module):
    """Character-level text generation RNN."""
    
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, hidden_size):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, hidden_size)
        self.rnn = nn.RNN(hidden_size, hidden_size, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_size, vocab_size)
    
    def forward(self, x, hidden=None):
        x = self.embedding(x)
        output, hidden = self.rnn(x, hidden)
        output = self.fc(output)
        return output, hidden
    
    def generate(self, start_char, length=100, temperature=1.0):
        """Generate text character by character."""
        generated = [start_char]
        hidden = None
        
        for _ in range(length):
            x = torch.tensor([[generated[-1]]])
            output, hidden = self.forward(x, hidden)
            
            # Sample from distribution
            probs = torch.softmax(output[0, -1] / temperature, dim=0)
            next_char = torch.multinomial(probs, 1).item()
            
            generated.append(next_char)
        
        return generated

print("\n💡 When to Use RNNs:")
```

✅ Use RNNs when:
- Sequential data with temporal dependencies
- Variable-length inputs/outputs
- Order matters
- Need to maintain state/memory

❌ Consider alternatives when:
- Very long sequences (>100 steps) → Use LSTM/GRU
- Parallel processing needed → Use Transformers
- Fixed-length sequences → CNNs might work
- No temporal structure → Use feedforward networks

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
### RNN Fundamentals:

| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Hidden State** | h_t = tanh(W_hh·h_{t-1} + W_xh·x_t) |
| **Parameter Sharing** | Same W across all timesteps |
| **BPTT** | Backprop through unrolled sequence |
| **Vanishing Gradient** | Gradients decay exponentially with time |

### PyTorch Quick Reference:

```python
# Simple RNN
rnn = nn.RNN(input_size, hidden_size, num_layers, batch_first=True)
output, h_n = rnn(x)

# RNN cell (manual unrolling)
rnn_cell = nn.RNNCell(input_size, hidden_size)
h_t = rnn_cell(x_t, h_prev)
```

### Limitations:

- ❌ **Vanishing gradients**: Can't learn long-term dependencies (>10-20 steps)
- ❌ **Sequential processing**: Slow, can't parallelize
- ❌ **Limited memory**: Forgets distant past

### Solutions (Next Topics):
- ✅ **LSTM**: Solves vanishing gradients with gates
- ✅ **GRU**: Simpler alternative to LSTM
- ✅ **Bidirectional**: Process sequence both ways

**Next Topic:** LSTM - The memory champion! 🧠
